title: Genesis Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who was the king of Shinar during the events of Genesis 14?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:1 identifies Amraphel as the king of Shinar during these events.

questions.question: Which king was NOT listed as one of the kings who made war with Bera king of Sodom?
questions.explanation: Chedorlaomer is one of the kings making war, not one of those who were attacked. Genesis 14:2 lists Bera, Birsha, Shinab, Shember, and the king of Bela as those who were at war with Chedorlaomer and others.

questions.question: Where did the battle between the kings take place?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:3 states that all the kings joined together in the vale of Siddim, which is the salt sea.

questions.question: How many years did the kings serve Chedorlaomer before rebelling?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:4 states that they served Chedorlaomer for twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth year.

questions.question: Which group was smitten by Chedorlaomer and his allies in Ashteroth Karnaim?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:5 mentions that Chedorlaomer and the kings with him smote the Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim.

questions.question: True or False: The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fought against Chedorlaomer in the vale of Siddim.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:8 confirms that the king of Sodom, king of Gomorrah, and others joined battle with Chedorlaomer in the vale of Siddim.

questions.question: Which king was NOT one of the four kings allied with Chedorlaomer?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:9 lists the four kings with Chedorlaomer as Amraphel, Tidal, Arioch, and Chedorlaomer himself. Bera was king of Sodom, opposing them.

questions.question: True or False: The vale of Siddim was full of slimepits where some kings fled and fell.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:10 states the vale of Siddim was full of slimepits and that the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell there.

questions.question: Who was taken captive during the battle according to Genesis 14?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:12 says they took Lot, Abram's brother's son, captive during the conflict.

questions.question: True or False: The kings who rebelled against Chedorlaomer served him for fourteen years before rebelling.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:4 states they served Chedorlaomer twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth year, not fourteen.

questions.question: What was the name of the king of Bela, which is also called Zoar?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:2 and 14:8 identify the king of Bela, which is the same as Zoar.

questions.question: Who was the king of Ellasar mentioned in Genesis 14?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:1 lists Arioch as the king of Ellasar.

questions.question: Which group was NOT smitten by Chedorlaomer and his allies according to Genesis 14:5-7?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:5-7 lists Rephaims, Zuzims, Emims, Horites, Amalekites, and Amorites as smitten. Sodomites are not mentioned as being smitten here.

questions.question: True or False: The kings of Admah and Zeboiim joined the battle with the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:8 confirms that the king of Admah and the king of Zeboiim joined the battle with the king of Sodom and Gomorrah.

questions.question: In Genesis 14, which event came first?
options: The battle in the vale of Siddim
The kings serving Chedorlaomer for twelve years
questions.correctAnswer: The kings serving Chedorlaomer for twelve years
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:4 states the kings served Chedorlaomer twelve years before rebelling. The smiting and battle come after the rebellion.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How many kings fought together against the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah according to Genesis 14:9?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:9 states that Chedorlaomer, Tidal, Amraphel, and Arioch were four kings with five kings they fought against.

questions.question: What was the condition of the vale of Siddim during the battle, and what happened to the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah?
options: The vale was full of slimepits; the kings fled and some fell into the pits
The vale was dry and sandy; the kings fought bravely and won
The vale was flooded; the kings escaped safely
The vale was rocky; the kings were captured
questions.correctAnswer: The vale was full of slimepits; the kings fled and some fell into the pits
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:10 reports that the vale of Siddim was full of slimepits and that the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, falling into the pits, while others fled to the mountains.

questions.question: After the battle in the vale of Siddim, what did the victorious kings take from Sodom and Gomorrah?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:11 specifies that the victors took all the goods and victuals of Sodom and Gomorrah and then departed.

questions.question: Who was taken captive during the conflict and what relation was he to Abram?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:12 tells us that Lot, Abram's brother's son, was taken captive along with his goods.

questions.question: Who informed Abram about Lot's captivity, and where did Abram live at that time?
options: One who had escaped told Abram, who dwelt in the plain of Mamre
Messengers from Sodom told Abram, who dwelt in Ur
Lot himself sent word to Abram, who dwelt in Haran
The king of Sodom informed Abram, who dwelt in Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: One who had escaped told Abram, who dwelt in the plain of Mamre
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:13 explains that a survivor came to tell Abram, who was living in the plain of Mamre the Amorite, about Lot's capture.

questions.question: How many trained servants did Abram arm to pursue the captors of Lot, and what does this demonstrate about Abram's leadership?
options: Three hundred and eighteen; showing his readiness and faith in action
One thousand; showing his overwhelming force
Fifty; showing his reliance on others
questions.correctAnswer: Three hundred and eighteen; showing his readiness and faith in action
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:14 states Abram armed 318 trained servants born in his house, demonstrating his decisive and faithful leadership to rescue Lot.

questions.question: What strategy did Abram use during the pursuit of the enemy, and where did he chase them to?
options: Divided his forces by night and pursued them to Hobah near Damascus
Attacked during the day and chased them to Jericho
Waited for reinforcements and chased them to Hebron
Sent spies ahead and chased them to Nineveh
questions.correctAnswer: Divided his forces by night and pursued them to Hobah near Damascus
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:15 reveals Abram divided himself and his servants by night, striking the enemy and pursuing them to Hobah, near Damascus.

questions.question: What did Abram accomplish after defeating the kings who took Lot captive?
options: He brought back all the goods, Lot, the women, and the people
He only rescued Lot and left the goods
He destroyed all the captured goods
He made a treaty with the enemy kings
questions.correctAnswer: He brought back all the goods, Lot, the women, and the people
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:16 states that Abram recovered all goods, Lot, the women, and the people, showing his comprehensive rescue.

questions.question: How does Genesis 14:10–12 illustrate the consequences of rebellion and the importance of trusting God in adversity?
options: The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and lost possessions, but Abram trusted God and rescued Lot
The kings won because they trusted their armies, and Abram failed
The cities were destroyed immediately without any rescue
Abram ignored the situation and remained passive
questions.correctAnswer: The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and lost possessions, but Abram trusted God and rescued Lot
questions.explanation: Verses 10-12 show the fleeing kings lost their goods and Lot was captured, but Abram’s faith and action led to Lot’s rescue, teaching trust and obedience.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 14:14–16, what biblical virtue is demonstrated by Abram's response to Lot’s captivity?
questions.explanation: Abram’s arming of servants and night pursuit shows faith paired with courage and action to restore justice, as seen in verses 14-16.

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 14:9, Tidal was described as the king of nations.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:9 identifies Tidal as the king of nations, along with the other kings involved in the battle.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 14:12 states that Abram himself was taken captive by the kings when they raided Sodom.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:12 says Lot, Abram's brother's son, was taken captive, not Abram himself.

questions.question: True or False: Abram's refusal to take anything from the king of Sodom demonstrates his integrity and trust in God’s provision.
questions.explanation: Though this is from later in the chapter (verse 23), it connects to Abram’s character shown in verses 14-16 where his faith leads to honorable action.

questions.question: What does Genesis 14:13 promise will happen if the reader follows Abram's example in verse 14 to take action in faith when facing adversity?
options: God will empower to pursue and rescue what is lost
Only prayer without action is needed
questions.correctAnswer: God will empower to pursue and rescue what is lost
questions.explanation: Verse 13 shows an escapee reporting to Abram, and verse 14 shows Abram pursuing and rescuing Lot, teaching that faith and action bring deliverance.

questions.question: What lesson about generosity and humility can be learned from Abram's conduct after the battle as described in Genesis 14:16?
options: Abram restored everything he recovered without selfishness
Abram kept all the spoils for himself
Abram demanded a ransom for Lot's release
Abram ignored the goods and only focused on people
questions.correctAnswer: Abram restored everything he recovered without selfishness
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:16 shows Abram brought back all goods, Lot, women, and people, reflecting generosity and humility in victory.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 14.

questions.question: Who met Abram after his return from the battle in Genesis 14?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:17 states that the king of Sodom went out to meet Abram after his return from the slaughter of Chedorlaomer and the kings with him.

questions.question: What items did Melchizedek bring forth to Abram?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:18 says Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine and was priest of the most high God.

questions.question: Melchizedek is described as the priest of which God?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:18 identifies Melchizedek as the priest of the most high God, emphasizing his role as a worshiper of the supreme deity.

questions.question: What blessing did Melchizedek pronounce over Abram?
options: Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth
Blessed be Abram, the mighty warrior
Blessed be Abram, king of Salem
Blessed be Abram, father of many nations
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:19 records Melchizedek blessing Abram as blessed by the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth, highlighting Abram's divine favor.

questions.question: According to Genesis 14, what did Abram give to Melchizedek?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:20 states Abram gave Melchizedek tithes of all, indicating Abram's recognition of Melchizedek's priestly authority.

questions.question: What was Abram's response to the king of Sodom's request to keep the goods?
options: I will not take anything from you
I will take all the goods
I will share the goods equally
I will return the goods to you
questions.correctAnswer: I will not take anything from you
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:23 records Abram refusing to take anything from the king of Sodom to prevent the king from claiming he made Abram rich.

questions.question: What did Abram say he would only accept from the king of Sodom?
options: That which the young men have eaten and the portion of Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre
questions.correctAnswer: That which the young men have eaten and the portion of Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:24 states Abram would only accept what his men had eaten and the share of his allies Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre.

questions.question: Which of these kings was NOT part of the four kings who fought in the war described in Genesis 14?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:9 lists the four kings as Chedorlaomer, Tidal, Amraphel, and Arioch, while Bera was one of the kings defeated by them.

questions.question: True or False: The valley where the battle took place is also known as the king's dale.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:17 refers to the valley of Shaveh as the king's dale, the place where the king of Sodom met Abram after the battle.

questions.question: True or False: Abram accepted the goods from the king of Sodom as a reward for his victory.
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:23 shows Abram refusing to accept anything from the king of Sodom to avoid the perception that the king enriched him, demonstrating Abram’s integrity.

questions.question: What is the significance of Melchizedek's offering of bread and wine in Genesis 14:18, in relation to later biblical themes?
options: It foreshadows the Eucharist in the New Testament
It symbolizes the wealth of Salem
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the Eucharist in the New Testament
questions.explanation: Melchizedek's bread and wine offering (Genesis 14:18) is often seen as a typological foreshadowing of the Eucharist instituted by Christ, linking priesthood and sacrifice across Testaments (see Hebrews 7).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage explicitly connects Melchizedek's priesthood to Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 7 discusses Melchizedek's priesthood and how it prefigures Christ’s eternal priesthood, connecting directly to Genesis 14:18-20.

questions.question: In the context of Genesis 14, what does the Hebrew word 'shoelatchet' (Genesis 14:23) mean?
options: A shoelace or even the smallest item
questions.correctAnswer: A shoelace or even the smallest item
questions.explanation: 'Shoelatchet' refers to the smallest article of clothing, like a shoelace, emphasizing Abram’s refusal to accept even the smallest gift (Genesis 14:23).

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in the blessing of Abram by Melchizedek in Genesis 14:19-20?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:19-20 uses parallelism by repeating blessings on Abram and the Most High God to emphasize divine favor and victory.

questions.question: Genesis 14 demonstrates an early example of which cultural practice common in the ancient Near East?
options: Confederation of allied kings for war
questions.correctAnswer: Confederation of allied kings for war
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:1-9 depicts multiple kings allied in war, a common ancient Near Eastern political and military practice.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which kings made war against the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela according to Genesis 14?
options: Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations
Pharaoh king of Egypt, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Cyrus king of Persia, and Darius king of Media
Saul king of Israel, David king of Judah, Solomon king of Israel, and Rehoboam king of Judah
Herod king of Judea, Pontius Pilate governor, Caesar Augustus emperor, and Tiberius Caesar
questions.correctAnswer: Amraphel king of Shinar, Arioch king of Ellasar, Chedorlaomer king of Elam, and Tidal king of nations
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:1 explicitly names these four kings as the ones who made war against the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by the rebellion and subsequent judgment of the kings serving Chedorlaomer as narrated in Genesis 14?
options: The doctrine of divine justice and human accountability
The doctrine of election and predestination
The doctrine of original sin and atonement
The doctrine of sanctification and perseverance
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine justice and human accountability
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:4 shows that the kings served Chedorlaomer for twelve years and rebelled in the thirteenth, leading to military punishment in the fourteenth year (Genesis 14:5-7). This passage illustrates divine justice working through human events to hold kings accountable.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is demonstrated by Melchizedek’s blessing of Abram in Genesis 14?
options: God as Most High, possessor of heaven and earth
God as a God of wrath
questions.correctAnswer: God as Most High, possessor of heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:19-20 records Melchizedek blessing Abram in the name of 'the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth,' emphasizing God's supreme sovereignty and transcendence.

questions.question: How does Genesis 14:14-16 demonstrate God’s providential care in the narrative of Abram rescuing Lot?
options: God empowers Abram’s servant army to defeat enemies and recover captives
God sends angels to fight for Abram
God causes the enemy kings to repent
questions.correctAnswer: God empowers Abram’s servant army to defeat enemies and recover captives
questions.explanation: Verses 14-16 narrate Abram arming 318 trained servants and pursuing the captors by night, defeating them and rescuing Lot, illustrating God's providential empowerment for deliverance.

questions.question: What does Abram’s refusal to accept goods from the king of Sodom in Genesis 14 reveal about his view of God’s provision?
options: Abram trusts God alone as the source of his wealth
Abram is unwilling to engage in trade
Abram desires to humble the king of Sodom
questions.correctAnswer: Abram trusts God alone as the source of his wealth
questions.explanation: In Genesis 14:22-23, Abram declares he will not take anything from the king of Sodom to avoid the appearance that the king made him rich, indicating his trust in God as his sole provider.

questions.question: Which nations are listed as being smitten by Chedorlaomer and his allies before the battle in the vale of Siddim?
options: Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, Zuzims in Ham, Emims in Shaveh Kiriathaim, and Horites in mount Seir
questions.correctAnswer: Rephaims in Ashteroth Karnaim, Zuzims in Ham, Emims in Shaveh Kiriathaim, and Horites in mount Seir
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:5-6 lists these specific groups and locations as the peoples smitten by Chedorlaomer and his allies prior to the battle with the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth emerges from Genesis 14:17-20 about the priesthood and kingship in the person of Melchizedek?
options: Melchizedek represents a theocratic king-priest foreshadowing Christ
Melchizedek is a fallen king seeking redemption
Melchizedek is a tribal chief with no divine authority
Melchizedek is a pagan priest opposing Abram
questions.correctAnswer: Melchizedek represents a theocratic king-priest foreshadowing Christ
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:18-20 shows Melchizedek as king of Salem and priest of the most high God, bringing bread and wine and blessing Abram, prefiguring Christ’s eternal priesthood combining kingly and priestly roles.

questions.question: How does the narrative of Genesis 14 connect to the broader redemptive story of Scripture in terms of God’s covenant faithfulness to Abram?
options: God vindicates Abram by delivering his enemies into his hand
God punishes Abram for intervening in human affairs
God calls Abram to leave his family again
God replaces Abram with another patriarch
questions.correctAnswer: God vindicates Abram by delivering his enemies into his hand
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:20 shows God delivering Abram’s enemies into his hand, demonstrating God’s ongoing covenant faithfulness which sets the stage for redemption history through Abram's seed.

questions.question: According to Genesis 14:10, what natural feature played a decisive role in the defeat of the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah?
options: Slimepits in the vale of Siddim
questions.correctAnswer: Slimepits in the vale of Siddim
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:10 describes the vale of Siddim being full of slimepits where the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled and fell, contributing directly to their defeat.

questions.question: What theological lesson can be synthesized from Genesis 14:12 and 14:13 regarding God’s involvement in human affairs and deliverance?
options: God raises up rescuers and allies in response to human crisis
God is distant and uninvolved in human conflicts
God punishes all family members equally
God favors only kings over common people
questions.correctAnswer: God raises up rescuers and allies in response to human crisis
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:12 records Lot's capture, and 14:13 shows someone escaping and telling Abram, leading him to rescue Lot with the help of confederates, illustrating God's providential raising of deliverers in crisis.

questions.question: What does the alliance between Abram and Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre in Genesis 14 suggest about the nature of covenant relationships in the ancient world?
options: Covenant relationships extended beyond family to include political and military allies
Alliances were temporary and lacked spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant relationships extended beyond family to include political and military allies
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:13 notes that Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre were confederate with Abram, showing that covenants included trusted allies beyond immediate kinship for mutual defense and support.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Genesis 14 is a mythical account with no historical basis. What does Genesis 14:1-7 actually teach about the historical and geopolitical context of Abram’s time?
options: It details a coalition of real regional kings and peoples, reflecting authentic ancient Near Eastern geopolitics
It is purely allegorical with no reference to actual kingdoms
It is a late fiction created to glorify Abram
It depicts supernatural wars without any human agents
questions.correctAnswer: It details a coalition of real regional kings and peoples, reflecting authentic ancient Near Eastern geopolitics
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:1-7 names several kings and peoples with specific locations, consistent with ancient Near Eastern political realities, supporting the historicity of the narrative.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Genesis 14:21-23 and 14:20 convey about the relationship between divine blessing and human integrity?
options: Divine blessing accompanies human refusal to gain wealth by compromise
Human wealth is the primary sign of divine blessing
Compromise with kings guarantees God’s blessing
Blessing is conditional on military conquest alone
questions.correctAnswer: Divine blessing accompanies human refusal to gain wealth by compromise
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:20 shows God’s blessing on Abram for victory, while 14:21-23 records Abram refusing goods from the king of Sodom to preserve his integrity, indicating that divine blessing is linked to faithfulness and integrity.

questions.question: What attribute of God is displayed by the phrase 'the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth' as used by Melchizedek in Genesis 14?
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:19 describes God as 'most high' and possessor of 'heaven and earth,' emphasizing His supreme sovereignty and transcendence over all creation.

questions.question: What narrative arc does the rescue of Lot in Genesis 14:12-16 contribute to in the broader biblical story?
options: God’s preservation of Abram’s family line for the covenant promises
The destruction of all cities in Canaan
The establishment of the monarchy in Israel
The building of the temple in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: God’s preservation of Abram’s family line for the covenant promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 14:12-16 shows Abram rescuing Lot, preserving his nephew who dwelt in Sodom, which is vital for the continuation of God's covenantal promises through Abram’s descendants.
